nameGame.title: The Name Game
nameGame.goal: Teach your dog to look at you when you say their name.
nameGame.step2: The instant they look at you, click.

sit.title: Sit
sit.goal: Teach your dog to sit on cue.
sit.step1: Hold a treat near your dog's nose.
sit.step2: Move it slowly upward and back over their head.
sit.step3: As their bottom touches the floor, click and reward.

down.title: Down
down.goal: Teach your dog to lie down on cue.
down.step1: Start with your dog in a sit. Hold a treat right at their nose.
down.step2: Lower the treat slowly straight down to the floor, then draw it a little forward along the ground.
down.step3: The moment their elbows touch the floor, click and reward. Repeat.

come.title: Come
come.goal: Build a reliable recall in low-distraction settings.
come.step1: In a quiet room, clip on the leash and take a few steps back from your dog.
come.step2: Say their name, then “come”, in a bright, happy voice. Crouch or pat your legs if it helps.
come.step3: The moment they reach you, click and reward — then let them go and try again.

stay.title: Stay
stay.goal: Teach your dog to hold a position until released.
stay.step1: Ask your dog to sit. Show an open palm and say “stay”.
stay.step2: Wait one second. If they hold the sit, click and reward while they’re still sitting.
stay.step3: Say a release word like “okay” and let them move. Repeat, adding a second each time.

leaveIt.title: Leave It
leaveIt.goal: Teach your dog to disengage from something on cue.
leaveIt.step1: Close a treat in your fist and let your dog sniff, lick, or paw at it. Say “leave it” once.
leaveIt.step2: The moment they stop and pull their nose away, click.
leaveIt.step3: Reward from your other hand — never from the fist they left alone. Repeat.

place.title: Place
place.goal: Teach your dog to go to and stay on a mat or bed.
place.step1: Put the mat on the floor and toss a treat onto it. Say “place” as your dog steps on.
place.step2: When all four paws are on the mat, click and reward — on the mat.
place.step3: Ask for a down on the mat, reward, then release with “okay”. Repeat.

calmSettle.title: Calm Settle
calmSettle.goal: Help your dog relax on cue, even with distractions nearby.
calmSettle.step1: Sit near your dog’s mat with something quiet to do. Don’t ask for anything — just wait.
calmSettle.step2: When your dog lies down on their own, say “settle” softly and give slow, gentle praise.
calmSettle.step3: Each time they stay relaxed a little longer, praise quietly again. Keep your voice and hands calm.

looseLeashFoundation.title: Loose Leash Foundation
looseLeashFoundation.goal: Build the first habits for a pull-free walk.
looseLeashFoundation.step1: Clip on the leash indoors. Stand still and wait until the leash goes slack.
looseLeashFoundation.step2: The moment it’s loose, say “yes” and give a treat right at your side.
looseLeashFoundation.step3: Take one step. If the leash stays loose, say “yes” and reward again. Add steps slowly.

jumpingFoundation.title: Jumping Foundation
jumpingFoundation.goal: Teach a calm greeting instead of jumping up.
jumpingFoundation.step1: Have a treat ready before you greet your dog. Keep your hands low and your voice calm.
jumpingFoundation.step2: If they jump up, stay still and quiet — the greeting pauses. The moment all four paws are on the floor, say “yes”.
jumpingFoundation.step3: Reward low, at nose height, while all four paws stay down. Repeat.

bitingFoundation.title: Biting Foundation
bitingFoundation.step1: Keep a chew toy within reach whenever you play with your puppy.
bitingFoundation.step2: When teeth touch skin, go still and quiet for a moment, then offer the toy instead.
bitingFoundation.step3: The moment they chew the toy, say “yes” and reward. Repeat.

crateFoundation.title: Crate Foundation
crateFoundation.goal: Build a positive first association with the crate.
crateFoundation.step1: Leave the crate door open with a soft blanket inside. Drop a few treats just inside the doorway.
crateFoundation.step2: When your dog steps in on their own, say “yes” and drop another treat inside. Leave the door open.
crateFoundation.step3: Toss a treat to the back of the crate. Each time they go in, say “yes” and reward. Keep the door open.

pottyFoundation.title: Potty Foundation
pottyFoundation.goal: Start a consistent, reward-based potty routine.
pottyFoundation.step1: Take your dog to the same outdoor spot right after waking, eating, and playing.
pottyFoundation.step2: Stand quietly and wait. As they start to go, say a cue like “go potty”.
pottyFoundation.step3: The moment they finish, say “yes” and reward right there — not back indoors.

dogWalksAway.guidance: Make the session easier. Move to a quieter space and reward one second of attention before asking for the full behavior.

dogJumpsForTreat.prompt: My dog jumps for the treat
dogJumpsForTreat.guidance: Hold the treat closer to their nose and move it more slowly, so jumping is never rewarded.

dogDistracted.guidance: Move somewhere quieter with fewer sounds and smells, then try again.

dogDoesntUnderstand.guidance: Break the behavior into a smaller step and reward that smaller step for a few reps first.

dogGetsFrustrated.guidance: Shorten the session and end on an easy win. Frustration usually means the ask is too big right now.

dogAlreadyKnowsThis.guidance: Great — add a small distraction or distance to keep it interesting, or move ahead to the next lesson.

bitingFrustrated.guidance: Pause and offer a chew toy instead of a hand or sleeve. Frustration during mouthing games often means it's time for a break.

bitingCausesInjury.guidance: This goes beyond what in-app guidance can safely cover. Please consult a certified professional dog trainer or your veterinarian.
